science.title: Common balance tests and their association with falls
science.description: Semi‑tandem, side‑by‑side, and full‑tandem balance tests are commonly used to evaluate balance performance. This study aimed to examine their associations with self-reported falls using nationally representative data from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (wave 1), including up to 57,720 adults aged ≥ 45 years. Balance performance was assessed using the 10‑second semi‑tandem and side‑by‑side tests, as well as the 60‑second (≤ 70 years) and 30‑second (> 70 years) full‑tandem tests. In the crude model, gender‑stratified weighted logistic regression examined the cross-sectional association between falls and ability to maintain balance for the full duration (yes/no). The weighted multivariate model was adjusted for age, grip strength, body mass index, activities of daily living, dementia diagnosis, and physical activity. In the crude analyses, significant associations were observed between falls and semi‑tandem, side‑by‑side, and 60‑second full‑tandem test completion ability (Odds ratio [OR]: 0.418–0.771). In adjusted analyses, significant associations with falls were found for male and female side‑by‑side test (OR = 0.527–0.622) and 60‑second full‑tandem test (OR = 0.784–0.856), as well as female 30‑second full‑tandem test (OR = 0.833). In summary, the 10-second side-by-side test and the 60-second full-tandem test showed the most consistent association with self-reported falls within the subgroup in which they​ were​ administered.

science.title: Orthodontic tooth movement-induced acute referred pain is associated with pain intensity but not psychological and behavioural factors: a prospective study
science.description: This prospective study investigated acute referred pain following orthodontic appliance insertion by examining the association between dental pain intensity (DPI) and orofacial musculoskeletal pain assessed using the TMD pain screener, while accounting for psychological and behavioural factors as potential confounders. Participants aged 18–44 years receiving fixed edgewise appliances (n = 121) and controls (n​ = 120) were recruited. Most included participants had mild psychological and behavioural profiles according to Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7, Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ)-9, PHQ-15 and Oral Behaviour Checklist-21. Follow-up was conducted via telephone on post-operative day 1, week 1 and week 4, during which participants rated DPI and completed the TMD pain screener. Fixed edgewise appliances induced greater DPI on post-operative day 1 compared with controls (p < 0.001), with no differences observed at later time points. TMD pain scores were positively correlated with DPI (Spearman’s rho = 0.21, p = 0.03) but showed no correlation with psychological or behavioural variables. Multiple logistic regression demonstrated that DPI was the only variable significantly associated with TMD pain score ≥ 1 (OR = 1.27, p = 0.047). Fixed edgewise appliances may induce transient dental pain associated with intensity-dependent referred pain in the orofacial musculoskeletal region. Clinicians should recognise this phenomenon to avoid misdiagnosis and provide appropriate management.

ai.title: Nvidia scandal: Corporate accountability at stake
ai.description: The controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is no longer merely about personal indiscretion. There are allegations that his affair with a Chinese businesswoman facilitated the transfer of billions of dollars’ worth of restricted AI (artificial intelligence) chips to China. The entire episode raises troubling questions about corporate accountability, national security and the concentration of power in global technology companies. According to media reports, a network of firms operating across China and Southeast Asia helped channel Nvidia processors, including those restricted under US export controls, to Chinese businesses. The alleged shipment of chips worth at least $7.5 billion indicates that sophisticated supply chains can become vulnerable to intermediaries and regulatory loopholes.
